title: AIMS Rwanda Program Manager Job 2026 in Kigali: Apply by August 31, 2026
summary: The African Institute for Mathematical Sciences (AIMS) is inviting applications for the position of Program Manager at AIMS Rwanda , based at its Centre of Excellence in Kigali, Rwanda . This is a full-time opportunity for an experienced program and project management professional who wants to contribute to Africa s scientific, educational, and economic development. The Program Manager will provide operational leadership and coordination for AIMS Rwanda s programs, including the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program and other donor-funded initiatives. The successful candidate will also contribute to partnerships, fundraising, program implementation, budgeting, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, and the long-term sustainability of the Centre. Applications will be accepted until August 31, 2026 . Opportunity Overview Organization: African Institute for Mathematical Sciences (AIMS) Position: Program Manager, AIMS Rwanda Location: Kigali, Rwanda Centre: AIMS Rwanda Centre of Excellence Employment type: Full-time Functional focus: Program management, partnerships, fundraising, education and development Application deadline: August 31, 2026 Reporting to: Centre President Primary working environment: Multicultural and international Languages: Excellent English required; French is an advantage About the African Institute for Mathematical Sciences The African Institute for Mathematical Sciences (AIMS) is a pan-African network of centres of excellence dedicated to postgraduate education, research, and public engagement in mathematical sciences and STEM. AIMS was established with the goal of enabling Africa s brightest students to develop the skills, knowledge, and independent thinking required to contribute to Africa s scientific, educational, and economic development. The first AIMS Centre was established in Cape Town, South Africa, in 2003 . Since then, the network has expanded across the continent, with Centres in: South Africa Senegal Ghana Cameroon Rwanda AIMS currently operates two Centres in Rwanda , contributing to the organisation s broader pan-African network. Each AIMS Centre provides tailored academic and non-academic programs and trains approximately 50 African students each year , preparing them for leadership roles in areas including academia, government, and industry. The AIMS academic model also brings together leading international lecturers who teach within an intensive 24-hour learning environment. About the AIMS Rwanda Program Manager Position The Program Manager will be based at the AIMS Rwanda Centre in Kigali and will report directly to the Centre President . The central responsibility of the role is to coordinate and oversee the day-to-day programmatic activities of the Centre. This includes responsibility for the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program as well as other programs and activities funded by donors. The position goes beyond routine program administration. The successful candidate will also help AIMS Rwanda strengthen its partnership network, support fundraising activities, and contribute to revenue-generating initiatives designed to support the long-term sustainability of the Centre. The Program Manager will therefore play an important role in ensuring that AIMS Rwanda s programs are properly planned, implemented, monitored, evaluated, and reported. Key Responsibilities of the Program Manager 1. Program Coordination The Program Manager will coordinate the Centre s day-to-day programmatic activities. This involves ensuring that programs are implemented effectively and remain aligned with their intended objectives. Responsibilities may include: Coordinating program activities Supporting program planning Monitoring implementation Ensuring activities are delivered on time Identifying implementation challenges Developing solutions to program-related issues Coordinating different teams and stakeholders Ensuring program objectives are achieved The position requires someone who can manage multiple activities while maintaining a strong focus on results. 2. Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program A significant part of the position involves supporting the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at AIMS Rwanda. The Program Manager will contribute to ensuring that the program is effectively coordinated and implemented. This requires strong organizational, monitoring, reporting, stakeholder-management, and program-management abilities. Because the program involves students and education, the role also requires an understanding of the broader relationship between education, development, and opportunities for young people in Africa . 3. Management of Donor-Funded Programs The Program Manager will oversee and coordinate other donor-funded programs and activities implemented through AIMS Rwanda. This requires an understanding of donor expectations and the ability to ensure that programs meet agreed objectives, timelines, budgets, and reporting requirements. The successful candidate will need to be comfortable working within donor-funded environments and managing the associated accountability requirements. 4. Planning and Budget Management The position includes responsibility for operational leadership in planning and budgeting . The Program Manager will work with the relevant teams to ensure that programs have appropriate plans and budgets and that implementation is monitored against those plans. Strong financial management and organizational skills are therefore important. Candidates should be comfortable working with budgets and using tools such as Microsoft Excel to support program planning and reporting. 5. Monitoring, Evaluation and Reporting Monitoring, evaluation, and reporting are important components of this role. The Program Manager should have a high level of comfort with Results Based Management (RBM), monitoring and evaluation (M E), and program reporting . This means the successful candidate should be able to: Establish and monitor program objectives Track progress against expected results Analyze program performance Identify challenges and areas requiring improvement Support impact measurement Prepare accurate reports Communicate program results to stakeholders and donors The ability to translate program data into meaningful information for decision-making will be particularly valuable. 6. Impact Evaluation The position requires experience and understanding of the impact evaluation requirements associated with foundations and international donors. AIMS specifically identifies experience with donors such as: Canadian Government Global Affairs Canada (GAC) International Development Research Centre (IDRC) UKaid USAID Other government and international development agencies Experience working within donor-funded programs and understanding donor reporting and impact requirements can therefore strengthen an applicant s profile. 7. Partnership Development The Program Manager will also support the Centre President in developing a strong and sustainable partnership network . These partnerships may exist at both: National level International level The role therefore requires someone who can communicate effectively with different stakeholders and develop constructive professional relationships. Strong networking and interpersonal skills will be important for building and maintaining partnerships that support AIMS Rwanda s objectives. 8. Fundraising and Resource Mobilization The Program Manager will actively contribute to fundraising initiatives. This may involve identifying opportunities and supporting efforts to secure resources for the Centre s programs and operations. The position also includes contributing to revenue-generating activities aimed at ensuring the long-term sustainability of AIMS Rwanda s operations. Candidates who have experience in fundraising, resource mobilization, donor engagement, or partnership development may therefore have an advantage. 9. Operational Leadership The Program Manager will provide operational leadership and oversight across the Centre s program activities. This requires the ability to coordinate different functions while ensuring that programs remain on track. The role will involve working closely with a multicultural team and interacting with students, staff, partners, donors, and members of the wider public. 10. Problem-Solving and Decision-Making AIMS is looking for someone who can make sound decisions and exercise good judgment. The successful candidate should be capable of identifying challenges during program implementation and developing practical solutions. This requires: Independent thinking Analytical skills Good judgment Creativity Flexibility A results-oriented approach The role is suited to someone who can take ownership of responsibilities rather than waiting to be directed at every stage. Educational Requirements Applicants should have a Master s degree in one of the following areas or a related discipline: International Development Economics Business Administration Project Management Social Sciences Education An equivalent qualification may also be considered. The academic background should provide a strong foundation for program management, development work, education, business, economics, or related areas. Professional Experience Requirements Applicants must have a minimum of five years of professional experience in program and budget management . This experience should include responsibility for areas such as: Day-to-day program implementation Program monitoring Budget management Program coordination Operational planning Reporting Program performance The requirement for five years of experience means that this is an experienced professional-level position rather than an entry-level opportunity. Project and Program Management Qualifications Professional qualifications in project or program management are expected. Examples specifically mentioned by AIMS include: PgMP PMP MSP Candidates with recognized professional project or program management credentials should highlight them prominently in their applications. STEM and Education Experience AIMS is particularly interested in candidates who have an understanding of education and development in Africa , with a strong focus on Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) education . Experience in education programs, STEM initiatives, development projects, or related areas can therefore be highly relevant. This is particularly important because AIMS s core mission is focused on mathematical sciences, STEM education, research, and the development of Africa s scientific talent. Gender Equity and Equality An appreciation of, or training in, gender equity and equality is also identified as a requirement. Applicants should therefore demonstrate awareness of the importance of inclusive and equitable approaches within education and development programs. Communication and Language Skills Excellent communication skills are required. Applicants must be able to communicate effectively in English , both orally and in writing. This is important because the position involves: Program reporting Stakeholder communication Donor engagement Partnership development Facilitation Team coordination Presentations Interaction with students and staff A working knowledge of French is an added advantage. Multicultural Working Environment AIMS operates across several African countries and works with students, lecturers, researchers, development partners, and professionals from different backgrounds. The Program Manager must therefore be comfortable working within a multicultural environment . AIMS is looking for someone with strong interpersonal skills who can effectively interact with: Multicultural teams Students from different backgrounds Staff Partners Donors Members of the public The ability to work respectfully and effectively across different cultures and backgrounds is an important part of the position. Results-Oriented Approach The successful candidate should be highly results-driven and motivated by a strong commitment to performance excellence. AIMS is looking for someone who can: Set clear objectives Establish realistic deadlines Monitor progress Deliver results Respond quickly to challenges Maintain high standards A strong sense of urgency and accountability will be important in managing the Centre s programs. Entrepreneurial Mindset AIMS is also looking for an entrepreneurial and self-starting professional . The successful candidate should enjoy working in a dynamic environment and be comfortable identifying opportunities rather than simply responding to instructions. This quality is particularly relevant to the fundraising and revenue-generation aspects of the position. Technical Skills Applicants should be proficient in the Microsoft Office Suite , including: Microsoft Excel Microsoft PowerPoint Microsoft Word Knowledge of internet-based applications such as Skype, Gmail, and similar digital tools is also expected. Strong Excel skills can be particularly useful for program budgets, monitoring data, reporting, and analysis. Who Should Apply? This position is particularly suited to experienced professionals who have a combination of: A relevant Master s degree At least five years of program and budget management experience Professional project/program management qualifications Experience with donor-funded programs Knowledge of monitoring and evaluation Results Based Management experience Strong communication skills Partnership development experience Fundraising or resource mobilization experience Experience in education and development Knowledge of STEM education in Africa Strong organizational and leadership abilities Candidates who have worked with major international donors or development agencies may be particularly well positioned for the role. The position offers the opportunity to contribute directly to an organisation whose mission is centered on developing Africa s scientific and mathematical talent. The successful candidate will not only manage programs but also contribute to broader objectives involving: African scientific development STEM education Postgraduate education Youth development International partnerships Donor-funded initiatives Resource mobilization Sustainable institutional development The position could therefore be particularly valuable for an experienced program manager interested in combining management, education, international development, STEM, and African development . Kigali serves as the operational base for the role, meaning the successful candidate will be expected to work from the AIMS Rwanda Centre as part of its full-time operations. Employment Type This is a full-time opportunity . The Program Manager will be integrated into the AIMS Rwanda Centre and will work closely with the Centre President and the wider AIMS team. Equal Opportunity Employer AIMS states that it is an equal opportunity employer . The organisation encourages qualified professionals to apply and is committed to considering candidates based on their qualifications, skills, experience, and suitability for the position. Candidates should ensure their CV and application clearly demonstrate: Academic qualifications Professional experience Program management experience Budget management experience Project/program management certification Donor experience M E and RBM experience Partnership experience Fundraising experience STEM or education experience Leadership and communication skills AIMS notes that if applicants do not receive feedback within five weeks after the application deadline , they should consider that their application will not be pursued further. AIMS also reserves the right not to make an appointment at its sole discretion. Conclusion The AIMS Rwanda Program Manager position in Kigali is a significant professional opportunity for an experienced program and project management specialist interested in contributing to Africa s scientific, educational, and economic development. The successful candidate will provide day-to-day programmatic leadership, oversee donor-funded initiatives including the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program, manage budgets and implementation, support monitoring and evaluation, contribute to reporting, develop partnerships, and assist with fundraising and revenue-generating initiatives. Applicants should have a Master s degree in a relevant field, at least five years of professional experience in program and budget management, and professional project or program management qualifications such as PMP, PgMP, or MSP . title: Communications Assistant Paid Traineeship at Friends of Europe in Belgium: Apply by August 26, 2026
summary: Are you a recent graduate looking to build practical experience in communications, social media management, digital content, website publishing, and events? Friends of Europe is offering a six-month paid Communications Assistant traineeship designed to help early-career professionals develop hands-on communications experience while working within an influential European think tank. The traineeship provides an opportunity to work across social media, digital communications, publications, website management, multimedia content, events, campaigns, podcasts, and communications administration . The position is based in Belgium and operates under a hybrid working arrangement . The traineeship is expected to begin in late September or early October 2026 and will run for six months, with the possibility of renewal. The application deadline is August 26, 2026, at 23:59 CEST . Opportunity Overview Organisation: Friends of Europe Position: Communications Assistant Opportunity type: Paid traineeship Duration: 6 months Expected start: Late September/early October 2026 Location: Belgium Work arrangement: Hybrid Team: Communications Application deadline: August 26, 2026 at 23:59 CEST Application requirement: CV in PDF format, no longer than two pages Selection process: One-hour online test followed by an interview for shortlisted candidates Possibility of renewal: Yes About Friends of Europe Friends of Europe is an independent think tank focused on policymaking and international cooperation. The organisation works toward a multilateral world where different levels of government, businesses, civil society organisations, and citizens can cooperate to address common challenges. Friends of Europe believes that effective policies and innovative ideas can emerge through collaboration, breaking down traditional silos, and creating communities based on trust. Founded in 1999 , the organisation works to stimulate debate, connect people, and encourage change in support of a more inclusive, sustainable, and forward-looking Europe. About the Communications Assistant Traineeship The Communications Assistant will join the Communications Team and support a broad range of communications activities. The traineeship is designed for people who have recently graduated and are looking to gain their first significant professional experience. Rather than being solely an observational internship, Friends of Europe describes its traineeships as an opportunity to combine initial full-time work experience with hands-on training . During the six-month programme, the successful candidate will have the opportunity to develop practical skills while contributing directly to the organisation s communications work. This could be particularly valuable for graduates interested in careers involving: Communications Social media management Digital marketing Content creation Journalism Public relations Website management Policy communications Multimedia production Events European affairs International development Think tanks and public policy What Will the Communications Assistant Do? The successful candidate will work across several areas of Friends of Europe s communications activities. 1. Editing Publications The Communications Assistant will help edit publications produced by Friends of Europe. This may include: Articles Reports Other written publications The candidate will be expected to ensure that content follows the organisation s in-house style and maintains a high standard of written communication. Strong English writing and editing abilities are therefore important for this role. 2. Social Media Management Social media is a major part of the position. The Communications Assistant will support the creation, planning, and scheduling of content across platforms including: LinkedIn Instagram Bluesky Responsibilities may include drafting social media posts, adapting visual materials, planning content, and supporting live event coverage. This means the role provides practical experience in managing social media communications within a professional policy-focused organisation. Candidates who already have experience managing social media accounts, creating content, writing captions, designing visuals, or analysing social media performance may find this particularly relevant. 3. Campaign Optimisation The Communications Assistant will contribute to the daily optimisation of communications campaigns. The goal will be to help campaigns perform effectively and achieve their intended objectives. This requires an ability to: Monitor campaign performance Identify useful insights Understand audience engagement Adjust communications approaches Support the achievement of campaign goals This aspect of the traineeship can help candidates develop practical knowledge of digital campaign management and performance optimisation. 4. Research and Insights The role also involves using different tools and information sources to uncover insights and develop strong messages. The Communications Assistant may therefore need to research information, identify relevant trends, and help translate findings into effective communications. Strong research, analytical, and information-gathering abilities can be valuable in this area. 5. Website Management The successful candidate will assist with updating and publishing content on the Friends of Europe website using WordPress . Tasks may include: Updating website content Formatting articles Uploading publications Publishing digital materials Making basic SEO optimisations where appropriate Experience with WordPress is an added advantage, although the role is also suitable for candidates interested in developing their website publishing skills. 6. Social Media and Website Analytics The Communications Assistant will help extract data and develop performance reports relating to the organisation s social media and website activities. The purpose is not simply to collect numbers but to identify useful insights and lessons that can help improve future communications. This provides an opportunity to develop experience with: Social media analytics Website performance Data extraction Performance reporting Audience insights Campaign evaluation 7. Multimedia Content The role also involves supporting the production of multimedia content for Friends of Europe s social media channels. This can include: Short-form videos Event clips Digital assets Other multimedia materials Candidates with experience in video editing, photography, graphic design, or Canva may therefore have an advantage. 8. Events and Live Coverage Friends of Europe organises events related to European and global affairs. The Communications Assistant may support communications around these events, including live coverage. Because some events can take place in the morning, evening, or on weekends, candidates need to demonstrate flexibility when required. 9. Podcasts The Communications Assistant will also assist with the conceptualisation, planning, and production of podcasts. This provides exposure to another form of digital communication and allows the trainee to develop experience in multimedia storytelling and content production. 10. Administrative and Communications Support The position also includes administrative responsibilities that support the Communications Team. These may include: Taking meeting minutes Managing correspondence Updating databases Supporting press activities Supporting multimedia projects Completing other communications-related tasks as required Skills and Qualities Friends of Europe Is Looking For The organisation is looking for someone who is motivated, organised, flexible, and willing to take initiative. Highly Motivated and Hands-On The successful candidate should demonstrate enthusiasm for learning and be willing to take an active role in the team s work. A hands-on attitude is important because the traineeship is designed around practical experience. Solution-Oriented Approach Friends of Europe is looking for someone with a can-do and solution-oriented mentality . Applicants should demonstrate that they are able to identify challenges and look for practical ways to solve them. Attention to Detail The Communications Assistant will work with written publications, social media posts, website content, reports, and other communications materials. Being able to meet deadlines while maintaining accuracy and attention to detail is therefore essential. Ability to Work Independently The candidate should be comfortable working both as part of a multicultural team and with minimal supervision. This requires initiative, responsibility, communication, and good organisational skills. Interest in Think Tanks Applicants should have a genuine interest in working for a think tank . An understanding of how think tanks contribute to policy discussions and public debate can help candidates succeed in the role. Flexibility The position may sometimes require attendance at events during mornings, evenings, or weekends. Candidates should therefore be willing to work flexibly when required by communications and event activities. Education and Experience Requirements Applicants should have demonstrable knowledge of and interest in communications. This can come from: A relevant degree Equivalent experience Self-learning Practical communications experience The organisation also welcomes candidates who have developed communications skills through practical experience outside of formal education. English Language Requirement Fluent English is required. The vacancy specifies that written and spoken English at native-level fluency is required. Excellent writing skills are particularly important because the role involves editing publications, drafting social media content, preparing communications materials, and supporting various written outputs. Social Media Experience An interest in social media is required, while previous experience is considered an advantage. Candidates should have basic knowledge of: Social media platforms Social media management tools Social media analytics Experience creating and managing content for platforms such as LinkedIn, Instagram, and other social networks can therefore strengthen an application. Graphic Design and Digital Skills Friends of Europe identifies several additional skills as an advantage. These include: Graphic design Photography Canva Video editing WordPress Applicants do not necessarily need to be experts in all these areas, but having practical experience in some of them can make a candidate s application stronger. Interest in European and Global Affairs Applicants should have knowledge of and an interest in European and global affairs . This is particularly important because Friends of Europe is a think tank focused on European policymaking, international cooperation, and global challenges. Candidates should therefore demonstrate an interest in current affairs, policy, international relations, European issues, or related areas. Who Can Apply? The eligibility requirements for this traineeship are specific. The position is open to: Nationals of European Union member states Nationals of European Economic Area (EEA) member states Nationals of Switzerland Non-EU nationals who already have the right to work in Belgium Applicants who do not fall into these categories may not be eligible for the position because the organisation does not indicate that it will provide work authorization for candidates who do not already have the right to work in Belgium. What Makes This Traineeship Valuable? One of the strongest aspects of the opportunity is its broad communications exposure. Rather than focusing on just one area, the successful trainee can gain experience across several digital and traditional communications functions. These include: Social media management Content creation Digital campaigns Website publishing Basic SEO Social media analytics Website analytics Publication editing Multimedia production Event communications Podcast production Database and administrative support This broad exposure can help a recent graduate understand how a professional communications team operates and identify which areas of communications they may want to specialise in long term. Hybrid Working Arrangement The position is listed as hybrid , meaning the successful candidate will have a combination of workplace and remote-working arrangements according to the organisation s working practices. Candidates should be prepared to participate in team activities, meetings, and events as required. Duration and Start Date The traineeship is expected to begin in late September or early October 2026 . The initial traineeship will last six months , with a possibility of renewal. This provides a substantial period for the successful candidate to gain practical experience and build a professional portfolio. Application Requirements Applicants are required to apply through the Friends of Europe website. The application should include a CV in PDF format . The CV should be: No longer than two pages Focused on relevant skills and experience Clear and well structured Tailored to the Communications Assistant position Applicants should also answer the relevant application questions and demonstrate their motivation for applying. Stage 2: Online Test Shortlisted candidates will be invited to complete a one-hour online test . Applicants should therefore be prepared to demonstrate their communications, writing, analytical, and practical skills. Stage 3: Interview Candidates who successfully progress through the test stage will be invited for an interview. title: World Bank Young Professionals Program (YPP) 2027: Fully Funded Global Career Opportunity, Eligibility, Application Deadline & How to Apply
summary: Interested in building a career tackling some of the world’s biggest development challenges? Join us for a World Bank Group Young Professionals Program (YPP) Information Session and learn more about the flagship leadership development program for exceptional talent from around the world. The World Bank Group Young Professionals Program (WBG YPP) offers highly talented professionals passionate about global development the opportunity to build technical expertise, gain international experience and contribute to projects addressing some of the world’s most pressing development challenges. What is the World Bank Group Young Professionals Program? The World Bank Group’s Young Professionals Program (YPP) is its flagship leadership development initiative for highly talented individuals who are passionate about global development. The Young Professionals Program offers a unique opportunity to build technical expertise, gain international experience and contribute to projects that address the world’s most pressing development challenges. World Bank YPP Highlights Global and competitive selection Initial start at headquarters followed by field rotations in various World Bank Group offices Initial two-year program followed by a five-year contract upon successful performance Working experience across the World Bank, IFC and MIGA through rotations Tailored training in coaching, mentorship and leadership Opportunities to engage with senior leaders and build strategic professional networks Exposure to global operations and diverse development challenges Program Features Rotations provide participants with broad exposure to global operations and diverse development challenges, ensuring a well-rounded understanding of the institution’s work. Beyond rotations, the program emphasizes continuous learning and career acceleration. Participants benefit from tailored leadership and technical training, dedicated mentorship and direct engagement with senior leaders, creating opportunities to build strategic networks and gain insights into high-level decision-making. Appointment Type: GF-level term appointment Duration Contract: The YPP is a 2-year program . Upon successful completion, participants are placed in a role for an additional 5 years based on performance , with the possibility of contract renewal. World Bank YPP Tracks Candidates may apply under one of two tracks: Operations Specialized Functions World Bank YPP Rotations The program includes three mandatory rotations of 8 months each , structured as follows: One rotation within your primary function and area of expertise One cross-institutional rotation At least one rotation must be based in a country office World Bank YPP Eligibility Requirements Education Applicants must have a minimum graduate-level degree or a higher qualification in a relevant field , completed before the September start date. Professional Experience Candidates need 2 to 6 years of professional experience in a related work area. If you are pursuing a doctorate, full-time doctoral research studies in a relevant field at an accredited institution may count towards the required work experience. The degree must be substantially complete, with all written work submitted before the September start date. Nationality Applicants must hold the nationality of a World Bank Group member country , as demonstrated by an officially issued passport or equivalent document. Language Proficiency An excellent command of spoken and written English is mandatory . Fluency in additional languages is considered an advantage and may strengthen your application. Employment Status You cannot be a current World Bank Group employee at the time of application (including term, open, short-term [ST], and extended-term [ET] appointments). You also must not have a close relative working at the World Bank Group or a spouse in a direct or indirect supervisory relationship . World Bank YPP 2027 Application Timeline Portal Opens September 1, 2026 Application Deadline September 30, 2026 at 11:59 PM UTC Late applications will not be considered. Interviews Assessments December 2026 – January 2027 Final Selection Notification Late January 2027 – Early February 2027 New Cohort Starts The new World Bank YPP cohort starts in Washington, DC, in September 2027 . Required Documents Applicants should prepare the following documents: CV/Resume — ideally 1 page, maximum 2 pages Passport Photo Page — confirming birth date and primary nationality Academic Proof — transcript(s) or enrollment letter(s) verifying postgraduate degrees and expected completion dates World Bank YPP Selection Process The World Bank Group Young Professionals Program has a highly competitive selection process. 1. Application September 1–30, 2026 Applications must be submitted by 11:59 PM UTC on September 30. 2. Longlist October 1–15, 2026 The full applicant list is reviewed, with the top 10% selected for the next stage . 3. Assessment October 15–31, 2026 Candidates may be invited to virtual interviews, leadership assessments and technical assessments. 4. Interviews December 2026 – January 2027 Panel interviews and case studies will take place in: Washington, DC Nairobi in December Paris Bangkok in January 5. Selection Candidates undergo a background check, with offers sent in late January 2027 . 6. Entrance The new cohort begins in September 2027 in Washington, DC. Is There an Age Requirement for the World Bank YPP? There is no age requirement for the WBG YPP. However, the program is designed for early-career professionals, so candidates must have 2 to 6 years of relevant professional experience to be eligible. What Can Successful YPP Candidates Expect? Successful participants can expect a combination of: International professional experience Cross-institutional exposure Technical and leadership training Coaching and mentorship Career development support Engagement with senior World Bank Group leaders Opportunities to build strategic professional networks Experience working on global development challenges The program is designed to help exceptional early-career professionals accelerate their careers while contributing to the World Bank Group’s global development mission. Who Should Apply for the World Bank Young Professionals Program? The YPP is particularly relevant for talented early-career professionals with a strong interest in global development, international development, economics, finance, public policy, operations, social development and other related fields . If you have the required graduate-level education, relevant professional experience and a strong interest in tackling global development challenges, the World Bank YPP could be an opportunity worth exploring. title: Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces Cohort 3: Apply for the 7-Week UNDP Online Volunteer Opportunity
summary: Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces – Cohort 3 Are you passionate about Africa’s development, leadership, public policy, education, entrepreneurship, community development, or the long-term vision of The Africa We Want ? The Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces – Cohort 3 offers an opportunity to take part in a structured seven-week online learning and volunteer experience designed to help participants understand how they can contribute to Africa’s transformation within their own spheres of influence. Hosted by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and delivered through the wider Agenda 2063 learning ecosystem, the programme focuses on turning knowledge of Agenda 2063 into practical individual leadership and action. The online assignment is designed for people who want to explore their personal contribution to Africa’s development while supporting other participants during the seven-week traineeship. It does not require applicants to be experts on every aspect of Agenda 2063. Instead, it emphasizes curiosity, critical engagement, communication, willingness to learn, and the ability to help others connect ideas to their own real-world environments. Opportunity Overview Opportunity Title: Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces – Cohort 3 Host Entity: United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) Assignment Country: Ethiopia Modality: Online Duration: 7 weeks Time Commitment: 11–15 hours per week Task Type: Development of plans Relevant Sustainable Development Goal: SDG 17 – Partnerships for the Goals Expected Start Date: The listing does not provide a valid start date Number of Assignments: 0 as indicated in the provided listing Language: English, fluent level desirable Deadline: No application deadline is specified in the provided opportunity details What Is Agenda 2063? Agenda 2063 is Africa’s long-term development framework and vision for building “The Africa We Want.” It provides a continental framework for transforming Africa economically, socially and politically while promoting inclusive development, sustainable growth, integration and stronger partnerships. However, understanding Agenda 2063 as a policy or development framework is only one part of the challenge. Its implementation also depends on the actions of individuals and institutions operating in different environments. This is the central idea behind Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces . The programme recognizes that important decisions are made every day in many different environments, including: Governments and public institutions Businesses and private-sector organizations Universities and research institutions Schools and educational organizations Communities and civil society Development organizations Families Professional networks Entrepreneurship and innovation spaces Youth organizations Other environments where people make decisions and create value These environments are described as “Power Spaces.” The programme encourages participants to identify the Power Spaces available to them and consider how they can deliberately use those spaces to contribute to Africa’s long-term transformation. What Is Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces – Cohort 3? Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces – Cohort 3 is a seven-week online traineeship and volunteer learning experience designed to move participants beyond simply knowing about Agenda 2063. The programme seeks to help participants answer an important question: How can I personally contribute to achieving The Africa We Want through the spaces in which I have influence? Rather than treating leadership as something limited to senior government officials, executives or institutional leaders, the programme takes a broader approach. It recognizes that individuals can create value and influence outcomes from wherever they operate. A student can influence a university or student organization. An entrepreneur can influence a business ecosystem. A teacher can influence learners and communities. A researcher can influence policy and knowledge. A community leader can influence local development. A communications professional can influence public awareness and engagement. The programme therefore focuses on developing individual agency and helping participants recognize themselves as potential contributors to Agenda 2063. Main Objective of the Programme The central objective is to help participants progress from understanding Agenda 2063 to recognizing themselves as agents capable of contributing to its implementation . The seven-week journey provides a structured framework through which participants examine: The value they currently create. The future they want to help create. The changes required to move from the present toward that future. The leadership values required to make meaningful decisions. The routines needed to turn intentions into action. The future they want to experience as a result of their efforts. The lessons they gain and the changes they need to make going forward. This makes the programme particularly relevant to people interested in leadership, development practice, public policy, entrepreneurship, education, community development and African transformation. The Seven Leadership Tools Participants Will Develop One of the most important features of Agenda 2063 in Power Spaces – Cohort 3 is its seven-tool leadership architecture. Throughout the seven-week journey, participants progressively work with seven leadership tools. 1. Contribution Statement – What Value Do I Create? The first tool encourages participants to identify their personal contribution to Africa’s transformation. Participants examine their current Power Space and consider the value they create within it. This may involve asking questions such as: What am I currently contributing? Who benefits from my contribution? What capabilities do I possess? What problems am I helping to solve? Where do I have influence? How does my work or activity connect with Africa’s broader development needs? The Contribution Statement helps participants understand where they currently fit within the broader transformation agenda. 2. Moonshot – What Future Am I Committed to Creating? The second tool focuses on developing a sufficiently ambitious vision for the future. The concept of a “Moonshot” encourages participants to think beyond incremental improvements and identify a consequential future they are committed to helping create. Participants consider: What future do I want to see? What would meaningful transformation look like? What ambitious outcome would challenge current assumptions? What future is worth working toward despite present obstacles? The exercise is intended to help participants challenge the limitations imposed by present circumstances. 3. Delivery – What Must Change? Having identified a desired future, participants then examine what needs to change to move toward it. The Delivery tool focuses on the gap between the current situation and the desired outcome. Participants may consider: What is preventing progress? Which systems, behaviours or practices need to change? What obstacles must be addressed? Which changes are most critical? What actions can contribute to the desired transformation? This stage helps translate vision into a practical understanding of what needs to happen. 4. Leadership Values – Who Must I Be? The fourth tool focuses on the personal qualities and values required to pursue meaningful change. Participants reflect on the type of leader they need to become in order to make consequential decisions and remain committed to their goals. This can involve examining: Personal values Integrity Responsibility Courage Accountability Resilience Collaboration Commitment Respect for others Willingness to learn and adapt The emphasis is not simply on what participants want to achieve but also on who they need to be throughout the journey. 5. Leadership Routines – What Must I Repeatedly Do? A vision only becomes meaningful when it is translated into consistent action. The Leadership Routines tool helps participants identify repeated behaviours and practices that can gradually produce results. Participants consider: What actions must I perform consistently? Which habits will support my goals? What behaviours need to become routine? How can I turn intention into practice? What repeated actions can accumulate into meaningful results? This stage emphasizes the importance of sustained action rather than one-time motivation. 6. Letter from the Future – What Does Life Look Like Because I Succeeded? The sixth tool asks participants to imagine their desired future as though they have already achieved it. Through a Letter from the Future , participants explore what life looks like because their efforts succeeded. This exercise can help participants: Visualize the impact of their contribution. Understand the consequences of achieving their goals. Reconsider current choices. Identify actions that are consistent with their desired future. Strengthen their connection to their long-term objectives. The exercise links future aspirations with present-day decision-making. 7. Future Review – What Have I Learned and What Should I Now Revise? The final tool focuses on reflection, learning and continuous improvement. Participants are introduced to the practice of: Return → Review → Revise → Recommit This process encourages participants to revisit their leadership plans and assess whether their circumstances, experiences and capabilities have changed. Instead of treating the seven-week programme as an endpoint, participants are encouraged to continue applying the tools after the formal traineeship ends. What Will Online Volunteers Do? Develop familiarity with the seven leadership tools. Volunteers are not expected to arrive as experts. The assignment specifically emphasizes curiosity and disciplined engagement with the materials. Support Participant Engagement Volunteers will help support participants throughout the seven-week learning journey. This involves understanding the weekly concepts, questions and exercises and helping participants remain engaged with the programme. The emphasis is on supporting learning rather than simply delivering course content. Participate in Small-Group Learning Conversations Where assigned, volunteers will participate in small-group conversations. These discussions are intended to encourage participants to connect the leadership tools to their own Power Spaces. Volunteers should therefore be capable of: Listening actively. Encouraging participation. Asking constructive questions. Helping participants connect concepts to their own experiences. Providing concise and useful feedback. Supporting a collaborative learning environment. Contribute to the End-of-Cohort Review Volunteers will also participate in a structured review at the end of the cohort. They will help identify: What worked well. What challenges participants experienced. What could be improved. Which learning approaches were effective. How future cohorts could be strengthened. How the materials and participant experience could be improved. This means volunteers can contribute not only to the current cohort but also to the continued development of the programme. Who Can Apply? The opportunity welcomes applications from people with an interest in Africa’s transformation and related areas. Relevant areas include: Agenda 2063 African development Leadership Development practice Public policy Business Education Community development Related fields Applicants should also demonstrate the following capabilities. Critical Reading and Learning Candidates should be comfortable reading learning materials and engaging with them critically. The programme requires volunteers to understand concepts sufficiently to support discussions and participant engagement. Strong Interpersonal Communication The role involves interaction with other participants, particularly through small-group learning conversations. Applicants should therefore be comfortable communicating respectfully and constructively with people from different backgrounds. Constructive Feedback Volunteers should be able to provide feedback that is: Concise Clear Constructive Relevant Helpful to the learning process Commitment Applicants must be able to commit to the assignment throughout the seven-week Cohort 3 period. The expected workload is 11–15 hours per week , making it important for applicants to assess their availability before applying. Language Requirement The listed language requirement is: English – Fluent, desirable. Applicants should therefore be able to comfortably understand and engage with English-language learning materials and participate effectively in written and interpersonal communication. Programme Modality and Time Commitment The assignment is conducted entirely online . This makes it suitable for participants who can contribute remotely without needing to relocate to Ethiopia or another physical programme location. The expected commitment is: 11–15 hours per week for seven weeks. Applicants should ensure they have sufficient time to: Study the learning materials. Participate in learning conversations. Support participant engagement. Complete assigned activities. Contribute to the end-of-cohort review. What Makes This Opportunity Different? One of the distinctive features of the programme is that it does not simply present Agenda 2063 as something participants should know. Instead, it asks participants to consider how they can personally contribute to its implementation. Leadership Portfolio and Letter from the Future Participants are expected to retain important outputs from the learning journey, including their Leadership Portfolio and Letter from the Future . These materials can serve as practical references after the seven-week programme. Rather than treating leadership development as a one-time training activity, the programme encourages participants to revisit their materials periodically as their circumstances, experience, capabilities and Power Spaces evolve. This creates an opportunity for continuous reflection and development. Contribution to Future Cohorts Another important aspect of Cohort 3 is its contribution to the continued improvement of the programme. Connection to Sustainable Development Goal 17 The assignment is linked to Sustainable Development Goal 17: Partnerships for the Goals . SDG 17 emphasizes the importance of partnerships in achieving sustainable development. The connection is particularly relevant because Agenda 2063 implementation requires collaboration among governments, businesses, communities, civil society, educational institutions, development organizations and individuals. By encouraging people to identify their Power Spaces and collaborate across different environments, the programme reinforces the importance of partnerships in achieving long-term development objectives. title: CDC Advancing Active People, Healthy Nation Through Science – Physical Activity Fellowship 2026
summary: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) is offering a research and training opportunity through the Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education (ORISE) for qualified researchers and graduate-level professionals interested in physical activity promotion, public health, community design, implementation science, epidemiology, data analysis, policy, and related fields. The CDC Advancing Active People, Healthy Nation Through Science – Physical Activity Fellowship , referenced as CDC-2026-0033 , provides an opportunity for an eligible participant to train with CDC s National Center for Chronic Disease Prevention and Health Promotion (NCCDPHP) , specifically within the Division of Nutrition, Physical Activity, and Obesity (DNPAO) in Atlanta, Georgia. This fellowship is particularly relevant to individuals interested in using scientific research, data, policy, community partnerships, and evidence-based interventions to increase physical activity and improve public health outcomes. About the CDC Physical Activty Fellowship The fellowship is connected to Active People, Healthy Nation , a national CDC initiative designed to help 27 million Americans become more physically active by 2027 . The initiative recognizes physical activity as an important component of population health and seeks to create environments and systems that make physical activity easier and more accessible. As an ORISE participant, the selected fellow will work alongside multidisciplinary teams at CDC and the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS). The training experience will involve research, evidence translation, partnership development, communication, evaluation, policy analysis, and dissemination activities related to physical activity promotion. A major area of focus is activity-friendly community design . This involves identifying, evaluating, and communicating evidence-based approaches that increase opportunities for people to: Walk Bicycle Use public transportation Access everyday destinations through active transportation Engage in other forms of routine physical activity The fellowship therefore goes beyond traditional exercise promotion. It examines how communities, transportation systems, policies, urban environments, and public health strategies can be designed to support healthier and more physically active populations. Research Project The selected ORISE participant will be placed within CDC s National Center for Chronic Disease Prevention and Health Promotion , in the Division of Nutrition, Physical Activity, and Obesity . The research and training experience will contribute to nationally significant public health initiatives that aim to generate, interpret, translate, and communicate scientific evidence. The fellow will contribute to efforts supporting Active People, Healthy Nation and may participate in activities involving: Scientific research Evidence reviews Implementation science Evaluation Policy analysis Data analysis Community-level strategies Evidence translation Scientific writing Dissemination Partnership development Public health communication The fellow will also have opportunities to work with experts and organizations across several disciplines, creating an interdisciplinary training environment. Key Learning Objectives One of the strongest features of this fellowship is the breadth of professional and research skills participants can develop. Under the supervision and guidance of experienced mentors, the selected fellow will have opportunities to develop the following competencies. 1. Scientific Evidence Reviews The participant will learn how to support scientific evidence reviews, coordination, and communication activities that may contribute to future updates of the Physical Activity Guidelines for Americans, 2nd Edition . This experience can provide valuable exposure to the process of reviewing scientific evidence and translating research findings into public health guidance. 2. National Partnership Development The fellow will learn how to engage with national partners in support of updates to the National Physical Activity Plan . This can involve working with organizations and stakeholders whose activities influence physical activity, health promotion, community development, transportation, and related areas. 3. Scientific Writing and Publications The fellowship provides opportunities to develop experience in authoring or co-authoring: Peer-reviewed scientific manuscripts Scientific reports Conference presentations Evidence summaries Other scientific communication products This is particularly valuable for candidates interested in establishing or strengthening a research and academic career. 4. Implementation Science Participants will build knowledge and skills in implementation science , which focuses on understanding how evidence-based interventions, programs, and policies can be effectively translated into real-world practice. This may include examining why certain interventions work in particular communities and how successful strategies can be implemented or scaled. 5. Evaluation and Dissemination Research The fellow will have opportunities to gain experience in evaluation and dissemination research. These skills are important in determining whether public health programs and strategies are achieving their intended objectives and how evidence can be effectively communicated to organizations, policymakers, professionals, and communities. 6. Policy Analysis The fellowship includes opportunities to understand policy analysis and evaluation related to community design and physical activity promotion. This can involve examining how policies and community-level decisions influence opportunities for physical activity. 7. Quantitative and Qualitative Analysis Participants will learn to apply both quantitative and qualitative analytical methods. Depending on project needs, this may include working with: Statistical data Qualitative data Mixed-method approaches R Python GIS Spatial analysis Emerging analytical approaches Candidates with existing data-analysis experience may therefore find this opportunity particularly relevant. 8. Interdisciplinary Collaboration The fellow will work in interdisciplinary groups and interact with professionals from fields such as: Public health Physical activity Tribal health Urban planning Epidemiology Community planning Transportation planning Policy Research This provides an opportunity to understand public health problems from multiple professional perspectives. 9. Qualitative Research The participant will build skills in qualitative methodology, including opportunities related to qualitative data collection, methodology, and analysis. 10. Data Analysis and Evidence Translation The fellowship will provide opportunities to analyze data and translate scientific findings into products that can be understood and used by different audiences. Participants may contribute to manuscripts and other materials addressing physical activity and community-level interventions. 11. Public Health Communication The fellow will gain experience developing materials such as: Infographics Fact sheets Evidence summaries Messaging materials Other communication products These materials may be designed for policymakers, public health professionals, leadership, professionals in other sectors, and the general public. 12. Presentation Skills Participants will also develop their ability to prepare and deliver presentations to internal and external audiences. This can strengthen communication skills that are essential for researchers and public health professionals. Preferred Skills and Experience Although the opportunity has specific eligibility requirements, CDC has also identified several preferred skills that can strengthen an applicant s profile. The preferred candidate may have experience in: Strong oral and written communication Scientific writing Peer-reviewed publications Scientific reports Scientific communication Teamwork Partner engagement Physical activity Active transportation Land-use planning Parks and recreation Related public health sectors Qualitative data Qualitative research methodology Qualitative data analysis Translating scientific findings into plain language R Python Tribal organizations and communities Implementation science Evaluation methods Mixed-methods research GIS/spatial analysis Community planning Transportation planning Data visualization Applicants do not necessarily need to possess every preferred skill. title: UNDP Early Warning & Preparedness Internship 2026: Home-Based Opportunity for Disaster Risk Reduction and AI Enthusiasts
summary: The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is inviting applications for its Early Warning Preparedness Internship 2026 , a six-month, home-based internship supporting the organisation’s Disaster Risk Reduction and Recovery Team (DRT). This opportunity is particularly relevant for students and recent graduates interested in disaster risk reduction, climate change adaptation, disaster management, humanitarian affairs, risk intelligence, artificial intelligence, digital technologies, early warning systems, and resilience building . The intern will contribute to activities involving risk intelligence, early warning, preparedness, anticipation, digital innovation, and artificial intelligence applications for disaster risk reduction . What Will the UNDP Intern Do? The selected intern will support several areas of the Disaster Risk Reduction and Recovery Team s work. 1. Risk Intelligence and Digital Innovation A major component of the internship involves researching emerging developments in risk intelligence and digital technologies. The intern may be expected to: Conduct research and analysis on emerging trends, methodologies, tools, and best practices in risk intelligence and disaster risk reduction. Explore developments in artificial intelligence, geospatial technologies, digital public infrastructure, and data ecosystems relevant to disaster risk reduction. Support the continued development of UNDP’s Risk Intelligence Service Line. Identify innovative approaches and document lessons learned. Contribute to the development of service packages and value propositions. Map and analyse AI-powered and digital applications relevant to risk intelligence. Research technologies such as machine learning, predictive analytics, digital twins, remote sensing, geospatial intelligence, risk modelling, early warning systems, and data visualisation. Develop knowledge products, concept notes, guidance materials, case studies, policy briefs, and communications products. Identify opportunities for applying innovative digital technologies within UNDP programming. This aspect of the internship is particularly valuable for applicants interested in the intersection of AI, data, technology, disaster preparedness, and international development . 2. Knowledge Sharing and Country-Level Good Practices The intern will also help identify and communicate successful approaches being implemented by UNDP Country Offices, Regional Hubs and partners. Responsibilities may include: Documenting country-level good practices. Identifying innovative solutions in disaster risk reduction and preparedness. Supporting dissemination of lessons and experiences. Engaging with technical institutions, research organisations, technology providers, UN entities, and academic institutions. Contributing to presentations and briefing notes. Supporting donor materials and proposals. Contributing to strategic documents related to partnerships and resource mobilisation. Preparedness Learning Pathway Another important part of the internship is supporting the continued development of UNDP’s Preparedness Learning Pathway . The intern will assist with: Researching and categorising resources for the expansion and tailoring of the corporate learning package. Supporting the development and maintenance of the online Preparedness Learning Pathway repository. Contributing to a self-paced course under the UNDP Crisis Academy. Researching resources for new thematic modules of the UNDP Preparedness Toolkit. This provides exposure to learning and knowledge-management processes within a major international development organisation. 4. Contributing to serious game methodologies under the Preparedness Learning Pathway. Developing social media kits for workshops and webinars. Preparing presentations, talking points, and briefing notes relating to UNDP’s global early warning portfolio. Candidates with strong communication, digital collaboration, and content-development skills may therefore find this component especially relevant. 5. Funding and project proposals. Briefs and talking points. Presentations and slide decks. Knowledge management. Communications activities. Other research and analytical assignments as required. Strong research and analytical abilities. Strong organisational skills. Excellent attention to detail. Proven proofreading ability. Ability to work with web-based applications. Familiarity with social media. Experience or familiarity with data management systems.
